sections.h2: What is the Town of Amherst, and which communities does it include?
sections.html:
Amherst is a town in northern Erie County and the most populous suburb of Buffalo. It covers 53.6 square miles, of which 53.2 are land, and the Census Bureau estimated 130,442 residents on July 1, 2025. Tonawanda Creek and Niagara County mark its northern edge, and Ellicott Creek flows through the middle.

Because Amherst is a town, not a city, the places people name in an address are mostly hamlets and mailing areas with no government of their own. The one exception is the Village of Williamsville, an independent village inside the town.

  • Eggertsville and Snyder, in the older southwest, near Buffalo
  • Williamsville, the incorporated village in the south
  • Getzville and the Audubon area in the middle of town
  • East Amherst and Swormville, shared with the Town of Clarence
  • North Bailey, around Bailey Avenue and Maple Road

Mailing addresses sometimes cross town lines. Some homes east of Transit Road carry a Williamsville address but belong to the Town of Clarence for taxes and schools, so check the tax bill for the municipality before you assume anything.

sections.h2: How did Amherst grow into the suburb it is today?
sections.html:
New York created the town on April 10, 1818, from part of the Town of Buffalo. The Erie Canal opened in 1825, and German immigrants settled the northern farmland while mills rose along Ellicott Creek. Williamsville dates to the 1810s, Eggertsville and Snyder to the 1830s, East Amherst and Swormville to the 1850s and Getzville to the 1860s.

The big change came after World War II. Census counts show 13,181 residents in 1930, 31,407 in 1950, 90,734 in 1970 and 129,595 in 2020. A town that tripled in twenty years likely has a large stock of postwar subdivisions, which is the kind of house many Amherst sellers now own.

Houses from that era often need updated kitchens, baths and mechanicals. Buyers who finance with a mortgage may push for repairs, while a cash buyer simply prices them in.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Amherst homes and households?
sections.html:
Amherst is mostly an owner-occupied town. About 69.9% of homes are lived in by their owners, and the median owner-occupied home is valued at $311,600.

More than one in five residents is 65 or older, and 86.4% of people lived in the same house a year earlier. Those numbers point to long-held homes, which often change hands through downsizing or an estate.

sections.h2: Which school districts and campuses shape buyer demand in Amherst?
sections.html:
Four public school districts serve the town, and the district matters as much as the street. Williamsville Central is the largest and covers the eastern half, including parts of Clarence. Amherst Central covers the southwest around Eggertsville and Snyder and runs Amherst Central High School. Sweet Home Central serves the northwest, including West Amherst and Getzville. Clarence Central serves a small southeastern piece.

Higher education adds renter and buyer traffic. The University at Buffalo's North Campus is in Amherst, along with Daemen University, an Erie Community College campus and a Bryant and Stratton College campus.

When you list or sell for cash, state the school district. Buyers search by district, and a house in one part of the same ZIP code can sit in a different district from its neighbor.

sections.h2: Which highways and roads connect Amherst?
sections.html:
Three interstates cross the town. Interstate 90, the Thruway, passes through the south. Interstate 290 runs diagonally toward Tonawanda, and Interstate 990 (the Lockport Expressway) lies entirely within Amherst and ends at Millersport Highway.

State and federal routes tie the neighborhoods together. US 62 forms the western town line as Niagara Falls Boulevard and continues as Sheridan Drive and Bailey Avenue. Main Street is Route 5, Transit Road is Route 78 on the eastern line, Harlem Road is Route 240, Campbell Boulevard is Route 270 and Sheridan Drive is Route 324.

The town's average highs run from 31 to 47 degrees from November through March and from 60 to 81 degrees from May through October. Winter is long, so roof, gutter and furnace condition get close attention during showings.

sections.h2: What rental rules does Amherst apply to a house with tenants?
sections.html:
Amherst Town Code Chapter 44 requires an owner to hold a rental registration certificate before renting out a unit. Owner-occupied properties with two or fewer units that are not short-term rentals are exempt. If you own a rental, these rules matter to your buyer.

  • A rental registration certificate is valid for up to three years, and the inspection fee is $75 per unit.
  • A short-term rental, meaning one to 30 days, needs its own certificate that lasts one year and is inspected annually. The 2025 registration form lists $250 per unit for owner-occupied and $500 per unit for non-owner-occupied short-term rentals.
  • The Town issues a certificate only after an inspection and a check that local property taxes are current.
  • An owner who lives outside Erie, Niagara and Genesee counties must name a local agent.
  • For a house built before 1978, the form asks the owner to certify lead paint disclosure.

A registration can pass to a new owner for the rest of its term if the transfer application is filed with the Commissioner within 30 days of the deed. Missing registration can lead to doubled fees, a $75 fine and a notice to vacate, and a violation can carry up to $1,500 and 15 days in jail.

sections.h2: How do assessment challenges and tax liens work in Amherst?
sections.html:
The Town of Amherst Assessor sets your assessment, and a challenge is filed on Form RP-524. The deadline in most New York communities is Grievance Day, usually the fourth Tuesday in May, which would be May 25 in 2027. Confirm the date with the Assessor's Office at 5583 Main Street in Williamsville, which has accepted paperwork by mail or drop-off in addition to in-person hearings.

Erie County can foreclose on county tax liens that have gone unpaid for two or more years. The latest cycle, In Rem 173, began on September 9, 2025, covered 2022 and earlier liens and set November 10, 2025 as the last day to redeem. Redeeming required the unpaid taxes plus a $500 statutory foreclosure fee, paid by cash, certified check, bank check or money order to the County Director of Real Property Tax Services. Unredeemed parcels go to public auction, and later-year taxes keep adding interest.

If you owe back taxes, ask Erie County Real Property Tax Services for a payoff figure, because the amount grows as fees and interest accrue. Closing proceeds can pay off a lien at settlement, so ask the title company to order the payoff early.

sections.h2: What does selling an Amherst house cost in transfer tax, and what are your sale options?
sections.html:
New York's transfer tax is $2 for each $500 of price, normally paid by the seller. Form TP-584 goes to the Erie County Clerk, and the form and tax are due within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

You can list with an agent, sell on your own or take a cash offer. Listing brings showings and buyer financing, and the closing date depends on the buyer's lender. A cash purchase takes the house as-is, which fits a rental with an expiring certificate, an inherited house or a property with tax arrears.

Before you choose, gather the deed, your current town and school tax bills, any rental certificate and a payoff statement from your lender.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental certificate to sell a house in Amherst that has tenants?
faqs.a: Registration is the owner's duty while the unit is rented. It can transfer to the buyer if the application is filed within 30 days of the deed, so give your buyer the certificate and inspection paperwork.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Amherst?
faqs.a: Most New York communities hold it on the fourth Tuesday in May, so confirm the exact date with the Assessor's Office. The form is RP-524 and filing is free.

faqs.q: What happens if Erie County tax liens go unpaid in Amherst?
faqs.a: The county can foreclose on liens unpaid for two or more years. Owners get a notice, a last day to redeem and a $500 foreclosure fee, and unredeemed property is sold at public auction.

faqs.q: How much is New York's transfer tax on an Amherst sale?
faqs.a: It is $2 for every $500 of price. On a $311,600 sale, which matches the Census median value, the tax would be about $1,248, because the tax rounds each $500 up.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Amherst house in?
faqs.a: Williamsville, Amherst, Sweet Home or Clarence Central, depending on location. Your tax bill lists the district, and the Assessor's Office can confirm it.
